ENVS456 - Computational Essay¶

Restaurants Inspection score analysis in San Francisco (2016-2019).¶

Introduction¶

In this assignment, I focused on the restaurant data, which will be able to tell about the qualities of the restaurants available in San Francisco lately. As far as we know, San Francisco is known for its renowned culinary landscape. The Forbes analysis has said that "what makes San Francisco a foodie destination is that the Bay Area has access to year-round fresh ingredients from both artisanal purveyors and local farms." It is also said that the Bay Area is one of the top dining destinations in the US. The forthcoming maps will explain the qualities, ratings, and many more characteristics of restaurants in the neighbourhoods of San Francisco.cisco.

Collecting and importing the data¶

APIs are Application Programming Interfaces that are required to bring applications together to perform a designed function based on sharing data and executing predefined processes. Talking about APIs, the API used here to make further analysis is called "Restaurant Inspection Scores (2016-2019)" from https://data.sfgov.org/Health-and-Social-Services/-Historical-Restaurant-Inspection-Scores-2016-2019/pyih-qa8i/about_data. The restaurants API used here is a type of Open/Public APIs that retrieves information about inspection scores, violations observed, and the risk categories of the restaurants in San Francisco. The data from the API helps to carry out an effective analysis of the restaurants in San Francisco, which has a renowned culinary landscape. San Francisco is one of the most popular places for dining decisions. The analysis in our report helps in the identification of areas or specific establishments that may pose higher health risks to consumers, facilitating targeted interventions to improve public health outcomes. Additionally, consumers can benefit from access to information about the quality and compliance record of restaurants when making dining decisions, ensuring they choose establishments that prioritise food safety.

Discussion of the data¶

The JSON library in Python allows you to parse and convert these JSON responses into Python data structures. Creating own API request using the requests library and sending the GET request to retrieve the Restaurant Inspection scores (2016–2019) The response is stored as Geojson, which consists of information on restaurants in San Francisco. The information retrieved can be useful for several reasons, such as finding a well-rated restaurant for consumers and tourists, and also for the public health and safety department to improve public safety. Additionally, the Shapefile of the Bay Area was downloaded to plot and visualize the data retrieved. The Bay Area shapefile was downloaded from https://geodata.lib.berkeley.edu/catalog/ark28722-s7888q. These boundaries help plot the coordinates of the restaurants.

Data Pre-processing¶

The restaurant data has been converted into a data frame using Pandas functions that have been imported at the beginning of the assignment, along with other useful libraries that will help carry out analysis in the upcoming parts of the assignments and plot informative and interesting storytelling maps. After that, the data frame has to be cleaned by removing all the irrelevant data columns and information from the data frame. Furthermore, the data frame has to be transformed into a GeoDataframe using GeoPandas functions. The shapefile downloaded has boundaries of Bay Areas that will be trimmed for the point of interest, which is the San Francisco region, and the irrelevant columns have been dropped since they are not required for further analysis.

Preparing the data¶

The Coordinate Reference System (CRS) defines how the projected map is related to real locations. The GeoDataFrame, which contains latitude and longitude as geometry with the help of CRS, Established CRSs captured by EPSG codes are well-suited for many applications. The CRS chosen for this datum and projections are epsg:4326. EPSG:4326, also known as the WGS84 projection, represents Earth as a three-dimensional ellipsoid. Since this CRS represents the earth in a 3-D ellipsoid, it is a common and widely used CRS for 3-D representation of maps. The reason for choosing this CRS is that epsg:4326 is a global standard that allows interoperability and consistency among different data sources and users.

The restaurants_score_sf is my GeoDataFrame, categorizing the restaurants as highly-rated, moderate-rated, and least-rated. Restaurants without any violations have been categorised as highly rated; restaurants with inspection scores lesser than have been categorized as least-rated; and the rest have been categorized as moderate. All these categories have been grouped by zipcodes to give an accumulative number of restaurants per category, which will contribute to our analysis throughout the assignment.

#categorize the rating of the restaurants with the inspection score 

restaurants_score_sf.dropna(subset=['inspection_score'], inplace=True)

restaurants_score_sf['inspection_score'] = pd.to_numeric(restaurants_score_sf['inspection_score'])

def categorize(row):
    if pd.isnull(row['violation_description']) and pd.isnull(row['risk_category']):
        return 'Highly rated'
    elif row['inspection_score'] < 80:
        return 'Least rated'
    else:
        return 'moderated'
        
restaurants_score_sf['category'] = restaurants_score_sf.apply(categorize, axis=1)
#print(restaurants_score_sf)

Static map 1 displays restaurant counts by zipcode (1–108) using a color scheme ranging from light to dark (purple), representing low to high restaurant numbers. The choropleth method in Folium is utilized for this visualization. It aims to emphasize areas with a large number of restaurants, possibly indicating popular dining spots or culinary attractions. The varying colors help viewers quickly grasp the distribution of restaurants across different zip codes, with darker shades standing out as areas of particular interest due to their higher concentration of dining establishments.

Static map 2 calculates the transparency levels (alpha values) based on the average inspection scores. It normalizes the scores and calculates alpha as the square root of the ratio of each score to the maximum score. In the map, the shape_group_gdf is plotted with varying transparency levels determined by the alpha values. The colormap 'YlOrRd' is used, and the plot includes a color bar indicating the values. The map visualizes how inspection scores vary across different geographic locations with transparency indicating the intensity of inspection scores.

mymap = folium.Map(location=[37.7749, -122.4194], zoom_start=12, tiles=mapbox_style_url, attr="Mapbox", control_scale=True)

def get_marker_color(category):
    if category == 'Least rated':
        return 'red'
    elif category == 'Highly rated':
        return 'green'
    else:
        return 'blue'

valid_rows = restaurants_score_sf.dropna(subset=['business_latitude', 'business_longitude'])

choropleth = folium.Choropleth(
    geo_data=shape_group_gdf,
    data=shape_group_gdf,
    columns=['ZIP', 'no_of_res_per_zipcode'],
    key_on='feature.properties.ZIP',
    fill_color='Greens',  
    fill_opacity=0.9,
    line_color='black',  
    line_weight=0.3,  
    legend_name='Number of Restaurants',
    bins=[0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, shape_group_gdf['no_of_res_per_zipcode'].max() + 1]
).add_to(mymap)

for idx, row in shape_group_gdf.iterrows():
    popup_content = f"<b>Zipcode:</b> {row['ZIP']}<br>No. of Restaurants: {row['no_of_res_per_zipcode']}<br>Average Inspection Score: {row['avg_insp']}<br><br>"
    popup_content += f"<b>Highly Rated:</b> {row['Highly_rated']}<br>"
    popup_content += f"<b>Least Rated:</b> {row['Least rated']}<br>"
    folium.GeoJsonTooltip(
        fields=['ZIP', 'no_of_res_per_zipcode', 'avg_insp', 'Highly_rated', 'Least rated'],
        aliases=['Zipcode', 'Number of Restaurants', 'Average Inspection Score', 'Number of Highly Rated', 'Number of Least Rated'],
        labels=True,
        style="background-color: white; color: black; padding: 10px;",
        localize=True,
        sticky=True
    ).add_to(choropleth.geojson)

marker_cluster = MarkerCluster(name='Restaurants').add_to(mymap)

for idx, row in valid_rows.iterrows():
    if not pd.isnull(row['business_latitude']) and not pd.isnull(row['business_longitude']):
        rating = row['category']
        color = get_marker_color(rating)
        popup_html = f"""
        <b>{row['business_name']}</b><br>
        <b>Postal Code:</b> {row['business_postal_code']}<br>
        <b>Inspection Score: </b>{row['inspection_score']}<br>
        <b>Violation Description:</b> {row['violation_description']}<br>
        <b>Risk Category:</b> {row['risk_category']}<br>
        <b>{rating}"""
        folium.Marker(
            location=[row['business_latitude'], row['business_longitude']],
            popup=folium.Popup(popup_html, max_width=300),
            icon=folium.Icon(color=color)  
        ).add_to(marker_cluster)
    else:
        print(f"Skipping row {idx} due to missing or invalid latitude/longitude values.")

marker_cluster.options['disableClusteringAtZoom'] = 15

folium.LayerControl().add_to(mymap)

Interactive map¶

The interactive map utilizes a monochrome basemap from Mapbox at a zoom level of 12 to ensure clear visualization of all areas of interest without overwhelming the user with flashy features. This choice prioritizes functionality and clarity over aesthetic appeal, enhancing the user experience. Polygons on the map represent the categorical distribution of restaurants within each zip code, enabling users to grasp restaurant density across different areas quickly. Popup functions provide detailed information such as zip code, restaurant count, average inspection score, and counts of highly rated, least rated, and moderated restaurants, ensuring easy access to relevant data. To prevent overcrowding and maintain clarity, restaurant points are clustered, with clusters disabled at zoom level 15 to offer a detailed view of individual restaurants in densely populated areas. Different colors are assigned to restaurant points based on their rating category, with green representing highly rated, red for least rated, and blue for moderate. This color scheme aids in quickly identifying the quality of restaurants within each area, facilitating informed decision-making for users. This choice balances the need for a comprehensive overview with the desire for detailed exploration. The use of a choropleth map to visualize the distribution of restaurants across zipcodes, with colors ranging from light to dark based on the number of restaurants, offers a clear representation of restaurant density. This visual cue helps users identify areas with high concentrations of restaurants at a glance, providing valuable insights into local dining options. Observations from the geo-visualization reveal notable insights into restaurant distribution. The zipcode with the highest restaurant count, totaling 108 establishments, stands out. Interestingly, within this zipcode, only one restaurant earns a highly-rated status, indicating a potential disparity in quality among the numerous dining options. Additionally, several zip codes, including '94103,' '94122,' and '94105,' each boast three highly-rated restaurants, suggesting pockets of culinary excellence within the area. Notably, the zipcode with the highest restaurant count also records the highest number of least-rated establishments, indicating a correlation between restaurant quantity and lower-quality offerings. These observations underscore the nuanced landscape of dining options within the region, highlighting areas of both abundance and disparity in restaurant quality.ality

Conclusion¶

Based on the data analyzed from the restaurant API focusing on San Francisco, it is evident that while the city boasts a diverse culinary landscape, there are discrepancies in the quality of dining establishments. The concentration of restaurants in certain zip codes does not always correspond to higher-quality offerings, as seen in the case of the zip code with most establishments but few highly-rated ones. This indicates a need for consumers to have access to information regarding restaurant quality to make informed dining choices. By identifying areas with potential food safety risks and disparities in quality, targeted interventions can be implemented to improve public health outcomes and ensure that consumers prioritize establishments that uphold food safety standards.
